title: Lesson Loop: capture what the coach knows at the moment they know it
one_line: A workflow and a business for padel coaches, and for any teacher with students: at the end of every lesson the coach records a voice memo, an agent turns it into a lesson note in the player's own vault, the player adds what happens in their games, and the next coach, or the same one, starts the next lesson from a two-minute briefing instead of from memory.

problem.name: The best picture of the player exists for five minutes
problem.text: At the end of a lesson the coach has the most complete picture of the player they will ever have: what went well, what did not, what to work on next. Then the next student walks on court, and it starts to fade.

problem.name: The player gets too much, and keeps little
problem.text: A lesson is an hour of instructions. "Focus on these three things in your next game" is hard to remember, and harder to follow up.

problem.name: Games never reach the coach
problem.text: Many players play better in lessons than in games, and the games are the point. Today nothing that happens in a match travels back to the coach.

problem.name: Every coach starts from zero
problem.text: A player who takes lessons from several coaches, or travels, gets several good perspectives and keeps none of them together.

problem.name: The coach's income is one hour at a time
problem.text: Most coaches work inside a club that owns the booking and the pipeline and takes a large, fair share. The relationship with the player ends when the hour does.

phases.name: Capture
phases.text: At the end of the lesson, the coach records a voice memo in Claude, ChatGPT or a transcription app. An agent turns it into a lesson note in the player's data vault. The player reads it. That is all, and it already changes both sides. Nothing else starts until this works.

phases.name: The player writes back
phases.text: The player adds match notes after games, and short clips. The coach can add clips from the lesson. The next lesson starts from a briefing that folds all of it together.

phases.name: Many coaches, one record
phases.text: The record belongs to the player, so it travels. A player who takes lessons from several coaches, or abroad, gives each a read key, and every coach sees every other coach's view.

phases.name: New revenue for coaches
phases.text: Remote video reviews, drill plans, follow-ups after matches, short content, and direct relationships with players who move or recommend them. All paid on demand.

exists.name: Voice capture
exists.text: Claude and ChatGPT apps take voice input, and transcription apps such as Otter record and transcribe. Phase one needs nothing else on the coach's side.

exists.name: An agent to process it
exists.text: The same assistant turns a transcript into a structured note with the prompt in prototypes/coach-memo-prompt.md.

exists.name: Vaults for the record
exists.text: sgit vaults are encrypted on the device, versioned, and opened in a browser with a key. A player's record is one vault; the key is the whole credential.

exists.name: Write-only lanes for coaches
exists.text: A vault append lane lets a coach add a memo without being able to read or change anything else. Documented at sgit.ai/api/append-lanes.html.

exists.name: Apps that call a model without a key
exists.text: A vault app can call a language model through the host, holding no API key, as documented on llms.sgit.ai. That is how a player's app would turn a clip or a match note into structure.

exists.name: Records the person holds
exists.text: The Supplement Stack vault on sgit.ai is a health record its patient holds; Health Score adds a clinician review screen. The player-held lesson record is the same shape.

streams.name: Lesson notes
streams.text: A voice memo turned into a lesson note and a player view. Paid by the player, or included by the club or coach in the lesson price.

streams.name: Match notes and briefings
streams.text: A player's match notes structured into themes; a two-minute briefing for the next coach.

streams.name: Clip processing
streams.text: A short clip turned into stills and notes the coach can react to.

streams.name: Remote video review
streams.text: The coach reviews a match clip remotely and records a memo back. The coach keeps most of it.

streams.name: Drill plans and follow-ups
streams.text: A personal plan for the next fortnight, or a voice note after a big match.

streams.name: The coach's own content
streams.unit: per item, set by the coach
streams.text: Short drills and explanations, bought one at a time rather than by subscription.

credit_note: Credits are bought on demand, for example £10 for 100, and spent on processing. No subscription. Coach services are priced by the coach, with the operator taking a share. Every price is a hypothesis.
domains: Personal training and physiotherapy exercise plans
Any one-to-one teaching where the teacher knows most at the end of the session
assumptions: A lesson note costs under 5p of model usage: a three-minute memo, a structured note back.
A coach gives about 15 private lessons a week, 4.3 weeks a month.
The operator takes 15 per cent of coach services.
Club variants, content sales and racket recommendations are not in the calculator.
